answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor identity in a bonded web of trust: from the kernel to a lone raven newcomer, each agent locks collateral and earns a voucher from a trusted peer before its vote counts. Weight grows with the square root of stake, so splitting one purse across many fakes shrinks influence rather than multiplying it, and every fake still needs its own bond and a distinct guarantor. Flooding an oasis of honest agents costs superlinearly: double the fakes demand far more than double the capital and vouches, while attacker influence barely climbs.
